## Phase 4 — Acceptance

I've moved from Facilitator to Implementor and built the real application in `implementation/` — fresh production code written from the behaviours we approved (not the throwaway prototype), with a Node server, a JSON API, per-account persistence via a session cookie, live page-detail fetching, and stored preserved copies.

**Verification is complete and passing:**
- **17 internal unit tests** — link/duplicate rules, the full search language (phrases, `#tags`, AND/OR/NOT, fallback), and import/export round-trips.
- **12 end-to-end acceptance tests** in a real browser, one per area, each asserting the behaviour we agreed for scenarios SCN‑001 through SCN‑017 (save/preview, correct, no‑duplicates, tags & formatted notes, search & filters, read/finished, empty & error states, open/edit‑address/delete, archive, bulk actions, saved views, preserved copies, import/export, sorting, and remembered settings).

**You can use it now at http://maker:4000** — it starts as an empty personal collection. A good tour: paste a link and confirm the preview; add tags and a formatted note; try the search box (e.g. `#tag` or `a AND b`); flip a bookmark to Finished; open **Select** for bulk actions; **Archive** something and restore it from the Archived link; save a filtered **View**; and open **⚙ Settings** for sort/copies/items‑per‑page/text‑size and Import/Export. Your data and preferences persist between visits.

**One honest note:** fetching live page details and capturing preserved copies depend on outbound web access from the review environment. If a page can't be reached, saving still works exactly as we agreed — you get a clear notice and can fill in the details yourself — and "Save a copy" simply won't produce a snapshot until the page is reachable. The logic and fallback are what's verified.

Everything is built strictly to the scenarios we approved; nothing beyond that scope was added.
